segment.description: Falling Water River mainstem, rising east of Cookeville in Putnam County and flowing through the Burgess Falls corridor (Putnam/White county line) to the Center Hill Lake backwater.
segment.boundaries: Headwaters near Cookeville (USGS 03422800 near Algood; 03423000 near Cookeville) downstream past Cookeville City Lake at Burgess Falls Dam (USGS 03423152 below the dam, 847.89 ft) and the Burgess Falls gorge to Center Hill Lake.

damTailwater.dam: Burgess Falls Dam (impounds Cookeville City Lake)

coldSource.notes: Elevation is the gage altitude (NAVD88) of USGS 03423000 Falling Water River near Cookeville, TN, from the NWIS site file. Tennessee Encyclopedia: in 1924 the city of Cookeville built a dam near the falls for municipal power, rebuilt in concrete after a flood; the hydroelectric installation closed in 1944, but the dam remains, creating a lake that is popular for fishing. No cold-release (bottom-draw/epilimnion) documentation exists for this decommissioned municipal dam.

holdover.detail: No trout stocking program exists for this river in TWRA data (the river is not on TWRA's 2026 stocking schedule), so no put-and-take holdover applies; no other holdover documentation found.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found in sources checked; the river is absent from TWRA's trout regulations page and regional descriptions of the Burgess Falls corridor mention bass fishing, not trout.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The river is absent from TWRA's 2026 stocking schedule and trout regulations, and the only dam on the reach is a decommissioned (since 1944) municipal hydro impounding City Lake with no documented cold release - no cold-water source or trout fishery is documented anywhere on this segment.
